title: Pax Deorum – a Roman city builder where you are also the city's patron god
author: keldareAI
selftext:
I'm working on Pax Deorum, a city builder set in ancient Rome with a twist: you don't just run the city, you're the deity it's consecrated to.

**The city side** is a classic production-chain builder. You zone housing, lay roads and raise workshops, farms and markets. Goods move by handcart from extractors through storage to markets to homes, and how well a neighbourhood is supplied decides which housing tiers it can sustain. Villa estates let you paint your own fields, orchards and pastures. I plan to keep the city size limited but have the citizen lead actual lives. This is because I want the citizens to be meaningfull when you rain your god powers on them.

**The god side** runs on Belief. Your citizens' faith fuels miracles you cast by hand: rain on a burning district, healing, or fire if you're that kind of god. What you do shifts your moral alignment, which has real consequences in the city (fearful citizen work faster for example but are more inclined to flee) and gates a talent tree of powers. Each Roman patron god plays differently.

**The realm:** your city isn't alone. Several fully simulated cities, run by AI governors, grow on the same map, and you can zoom out to a strategic view of the empire.



Most of the basic core of the game is there production,  building, citizen simulation, god powers and belief. 

struggled a lot with assets/visuals but since opus 5.5 and astra came out the quality improved a lot. Im confident future models will be able to raise the asset level to the bar im aiming at.

Opus 5.5 for example built the walkers ranging from citizen to legionnaires from scratch with my instructions in blender and animated them.

This is a screenshot of me dropping a fireball on my city, atm the walkers aren't yet responding but I plan to make them panic.

The buildings in the front are done by Astra and are nearing the level im aiming for but still lack detail. The ones in the back were done by opus 4.8 and were always very bad.

This for example is a market place (rendered in my own renderer) im going to allow to be placed with the road going through. the buildings in the back are not yet good enough but im pleased with the stalls.

  
Happy to answer questions. I'd especially like to hear what you'd want from the god layer in a city builder. So far iv tried to include god powers that are closely tied to the nature of the god your city is devoted to. For example if you pick Ceres you will be able to boost production of the fields, do harvest festivals or send plagues and diseases to wither the crops.
